target.statement: For the fixed operational data declared below, establish the conjunction that (i) for every monoid A the two-sided contextual relation is the coarsest response-compatible congruence and its quotient has the terminal finer-to-coarser factorization property, while only for finite A it has minimum cardinality and equality of quotient cardinalities forces an isomorphism over A; (ii) under compact-metrizable continuity and quotient-map hypotheses this quotient is compact metrizable with continuous multiplication and response; (iii) finite normalized typed local-kernel replacement with palettes compact in finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes supports a compact right-override soft protocol monoid with continuous response, and the retained mediator target face of the released BSC pair has unequal exact total-variation diameters despite the same passive law; (iv) independent randomized hard protocols form an affine convolution monoid whose released BSC contextual signatures have full rank, so equal passive laws do not determine the randomized response experiment under response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphism; (v) declared finite standard-Borel DAG kernels give Borel protocol responses and the compact-Polish jointly Feller finite-coordinate right-override tier gives a compact metrizable operational quotient; and (vi) with mediator palette `P(T)` in the weak topology and constant-parent kernels `K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE)`, the circle heat-kernel pair has the same passive retained law but strict one-way Blackwell comparison and strict soft response-set inclusion. Every admitted typed relabeling is induced by invertible typed state maps, a compatible protocol-monoid isomorphism `Theta`, and one protocol-independent boundary-response isomorphism `U` satisfying `Phi'(Theta(a))=U(Phi(a))` for every protocol. The BSC and circle comparison categories fix `R` as the input/parameter boundary and `O` as the output/observation boundary and forbid `R`-`O` exchange and time-reversal morphisms. No canonical raw latent/DAG realization, target-erasing arbitrary-soft result, correlated-randomization result, uncontrolled regular-conditional identification, noncompact topological quotient theorem, VFE/ELBO emergence, agency, gauge/RG extension, or ontology claim is in the target.
target.quantifiers: For every monoid A, response set Y, response map Phi:A->Y, and algebraic response-compatible quotient triple (q,B,psi) in which q:A->B is a surjective unital monoid homomorphism, psi:B->Y is a map, and Phi=psi∘q, the algebraic contextual congruence and unique finer-to-coarser factorization conjunct is universal. Only when A is finite, the quotient has minimum cardinality among response-compatible quotient triples, and equality of cardinalities makes the factor map an isomorphism over A. For every compact metrizable monoid A with jointly continuous multiplication, metrizable Hausdorff Y, and continuous Phi, and every topological response-compatible quotient triple with B a compact Hausdorff topological monoid, q and psi continuous, and q a quotient map, the compact-quotient conjunct is universal. For every finite DAG presentation with finite state spaces and declared typed palettes J_v that are compact subsets of the corresponding finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes with Euclidean/evaluation-subspace topology, the normalized soft-replacement semantics and response continuity are universal; the unequal target-face diameters are asserted for the specified BSC models L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4), every epsilon with 0<epsilon<1/2, and every interior pair epsilon<s_-<s_+<1-epsilon, with `R` fixed as input/parameter and `O` fixed as output/observation. For the released fifteen-class hard BSC monoids and independently randomized selectors, the affine-convolution and full-contextual-rank conjunct is asserted at passive crossover delta=5/12 under response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphisms that preserve that ordered boundary. For every finite standard-Borel DAG with standard-Borel protocol palettes and declared jointly evaluation-measurable normalized pointwise kernel families, the Borel-response conjunct is universal; for every compact-Polish jointly Feller instance whose protocol monoid is the finite-coordinate right-override product of compact metrizable palettes and isolated bottom symbols, the compact operational quotient conjunct is universal. For the circle heat-kernel models and every 0<s<t, set `J_E=P(T)` with weak topology and `K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE)`; the passive-equality, strict one-way Blackwell, compact-Feller, and strict soft-response-set conjuncts are universal in s and t, with a positive smooth strictness witness `nu_rho=H_rho(x_0,dot)` for every fixed circle point `x_0` and every 0<rho<t-s, where `dot` denotes the measure argument. Every admitted typed comparison is induced by invertible typed state maps, the compatible pushforward protocol-monoid isomorphism `Theta`, and one protocol-independent boundary-response isomorphism `U` satisfying `Phi'(Theta(a))=U(Phi(a))` for every protocol `a`. Every BSC and circle experiment comparison preserves the ordered `R`-to-`O` external boundary, declared target/type coloring, response codomain, mediator parameter experiment, circle heat geometry where applicable, and admitted morphism class; `R`-`O` exchange, time reversal, and protocol-dependent boundary intertwiners are forbidden.
domains: Arbitrary monoids A with identity, arbitrary response sets Y, maps Phi:A->Y, and algebraic response-compatible quotient triples (q,B,psi) with q:A->B a surjective unital monoid homomorphism, psi:B->Y a map, and Phi=psi∘q.

Compact metrizable monoids A with jointly continuous multiplication and continuous responses into metrizable Hausdorff spaces, together with topological response-compatible quotient triples (q,B,psi) whose B is a compact Hausdorff topological monoid, q and psi are continuous, and q is a quotient map.

Finite DAG presentations with finite standard-Borel node spaces, normalized baseline kernels, typed palettes J_v that are compact subsets of the corresponding finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes with Euclidean/evaluation-subspace topology, one isolated bottom_v symbol per node, and the finite-coordinate compact right-override product A=product_v({bottom_v} disjoint-union J_v), with `R` fixed as the input/parameter boundary and `O` fixed as the output/observation boundary; the product may have infinite cardinality.

The released fifteen-class hard intervention monoids for the directed BSC chains L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4), their probability simplices, and independently sampled sequential selectors, with the ordered external boundary `R` input/parameter and `O` output/observation retained.

Finite DAGs on declared standard-Borel spaces with standard-Borel protocol palettes and declared jointly evaluation-measurable normalized pointwise baseline and replacement-kernel families; and the compact-Polish jointly Feller sub-tier with compact metrizable palettes, isolated bottom symbols, and a finite-coordinate compact right-override product that may have infinite cardinality.

The directed circle chain with `R` fixed as input/parameter, `E` as mediator, and `O` fixed as output/observation; circle T with normalized Haar probability m and positive smooth heat kernels H_t for 0<s<t; mediator palette J_E=P(T) with weak topology and constant-parent kernels K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE); and the mediator parameter experiment and circle heat geometry compared only through the declared protocol-compatible global-intertwiner relabelings.
codomains: The syntactic response quotient Syn(Phi), its descended response, and continuous compact realizations through countable contextual signatures when the compact hypotheses hold.

Retained probability laws with total-variation geometry, affine randomized response experiments, and P(X_ret) with its evaluation sigma-algebra in the standard-Borel tier or weak-law topology in the compact-Polish Feller tier.

Circle probability laws and ordered mediator-to-output Markov experiments, with `R` input/parameter and `O` output/observation fixed, ordered by boundary-preserving heat-geometry-preserving Blackwell garbling.
target.regularity: Algebraic quotient claims require only total monoid multiplication and the explicit algebraic response-compatible triple. Compact claims require compact metrizability, joint continuity of multiplication, Hausdorff response codomain, response continuity, and a topological response-compatible triple in which q and psi are continuous and q is a quotient map; compact-to-Hausdorff continuous surjections supply the quotient-map condition. In the finite soft tier, each J_v is compact in its finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytope with Euclidean/evaluation-subspace topology, equivalently every kernel-coordinate evaluation is continuous; every retained-law coordinate is then a finite polynomial in those coordinates, proving response continuity. Finite randomized claims use normalized kernels and finite sums. Standard-Borel claims use standard-Borel palettes, explicitly declared normalized kernels with joint evaluation measurability, P(X_ret) with its evaluation sigma-algebra, and finite topological-order Ionescu--Tulcea recursion. The positive compact-Feller tier additionally requires compact Polish node spaces, compact metrizable replacement palettes, isolated bottom symbols, jointly continuous finite-coordinate right-override multiplication, and jointly Feller kernels; finite-coordinate does not mean finite cardinality. For the circle tier, compactness of T makes P(T) compact metrizable in the weak topology, and K_nu is jointly Feller because for every continuous f the map (nu,r)->integral f dnu is weakly continuous and independent of r. Heat kernels are the standard positive smooth Feller convolution kernels on the circle. No topology on an arbitrary all-kernel space and no pointwise version inferred from observational conditionals is assumed.
measures: Normalized laws on each finite or standard-Borel node space and the retained-variable product sigma-algebra.
Probability measures on each finite hard protocol set for independently randomized selectors, composed by convolution.
Normalized Haar probability on the circle and its heat-kernel transition probabilities.
Evaluation sigma-algebra on P(X_ret) in the standard-Borel tier and weak probability-law topology only in the compact-Polish Feller tier.
boundary_conditions: Universal congruence and factorization do not require A finite; minimum cardinality and equality-implies-isomorphism are asserted only when A is finite.

Finite soft palettes carry the Euclidean/evaluation-subspace topology inherited from their finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes; compactness without this evaluation continuity is not enough for the response-continuity claim.

Finite soft preparations use epsilon in (0,1/2); for every epsilon<s_-<s_+<1-epsilon the target-face witness is strictly interior and has separation |1-2b|(s_+-s_-), so it does not rely on hard endpoints.

The mediator target/type face and ordered external boundary are retained in the finite BSC soft comparison: `R` is input/parameter and `O` is output/observation; target-erasing, `R`-`O`-exchanging, and time-reversal morphisms are outside the theorem.

Randomized sequential selectors are independent and unmarked, response is affine, and admitted isomorphisms are response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphisms; correlated or shared-noise selection is outside the theorem.
The statement that boundary point interventions span the full retained simplex is restricted to the declared four-atom witness, whose four boundary point interventions are its four vertices.
Standard-Borel point interventions use declared pointwise mechanisms; arbitrary observational regular-conditionals at null conditioning values are outside the theorem.

Compactness, finite-coordinate right-override multiplication, and Feller continuity are additional sufficient hypotheses, not consequences of standard Borelness; finite-coordinate does not mean finite cardinality, and no noncompact quotient regularity is asserted.

The circle comparison fixes the ordered `R`-to-`O` external boundary, mediator parameter experiment, and heat geometry; `R`-`O` exchange and time reversal are forbidden. Strict soft inclusion uses the positive smooth preparation law `nu_rho=H_rho(x_0,dot)` for fixed `x_0` and 0<rho<t-s, where `dot` denotes the measure argument.
Response-law equivalence does not assert equality of fixed-observation ELBOs, latent posteriors, or generative factorizations.
symmetries: Algebraic quotient maps are surjective and unital and preserve response by Phi=psi∘q; topological quotient triples additionally require q and psi continuous and q a quotient map; randomized isomorphisms are affine convolution-monoid maps.

An admitted typed relabeling consists of invertible typed state maps f_R,f_E,f_O preserving the ordered boundary roles, the protocol-monoid isomorphism Theta induced by pushing every baseline and replacement kernel through those maps, and one protocol-independent boundary-response isomorphism U satisfying Phi'(Theta(a))=U(Phi(a)) for every protocol a; in topological tiers these maps have the declared continuity.

For the circle comparison, the typed state maps additionally intertwine every heat kernel, the same global U works for every protocol, and neither the state maps nor Theta may exchange R with O or implement time reversal.
Bare response-monoid automorphisms are not quotiented away when the raw quotient map from A is part of the universal-property data.
target.equivalence: Algebraic contextual equivalence is a equiv_Phi b exactly when Phi(uav)=Phi(ubv) for all u,v in A. An algebraic response-compatible quotient triple (q,B,psi) has q surjective and unital with Phi=psi∘q; triples are compared over A by maps commuting with quotient maps and descended responses. A topological triple additionally has q and psi continuous and q a quotient map. Presentation relabelings are equivalent only when invertible typed state maps induce a compatible protocol map Theta and one protocol-independent global boundary response map U with Phi'(Theta(a))=U(Phi(a)) for every a. Randomized comparisons additionally require Theta affine and convolution preserving; circle comparisons additionally require the state maps to intertwine the heat kernels. `R`-`O` exchange, time reversal, and protocol-dependent response maps are not equivalences.
premises: The released hard-intervention and canonical-selection packages at repository revision 53cafa374a668ea017a7c50ddbeb75e9045f73a8 supply the fixed BSC presentations and fifteen hard protocol classes but do not supply the new proofs.

The contextual quotient retains the raw protocol monoid A, response map Phi, response codomain Y, declared target/type coloring where present, and admitted morphism class as fixed operational data; every presentation relabeling uses invertible typed state maps, the induced compatible protocol map Theta, and one global boundary response map U for all protocols.
Every algebraic response-compatible triple has a surjective unital q and Phi=psi∘q; every topological triple additionally has q and psi continuous and q a quotient map.

Finite local replacement uses palettes J_v compact in their finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes with Euclidean/evaluation-subspace topology and the finite-coordinate compact product A=product_v({bottom_v} disjoint-union J_v) with isolated bottom_v and coordinatewise right override, where bottom_v means leave the declared mechanism unchanged; this multiplication is jointly continuous, the monoid may have infinite cardinality, and its finite-state response is continuous.
The randomized protocol monoid uses independent convolution on the finite hard monoid and the response of a selector law is the affine mixture of deterministic responses.
The Borel tier uses standard-Borel palettes, joint evaluation measurability, P(X_ret) with its evaluation sigma-algebra, and finite topological-order Ionescu--Tulcea recursion.

The circle heat semigroup is typed by H_s H_t=H_(s+t) and acts on Fourier modes by H_t e_n=exp(-n^2 t)e_n. Its mediator soft palette is P(T) with weak topology and K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE); compactness of T and weak continuity of integration make this a compact jointly Feller palette. The comparison category fixes `R` as input/parameter, `O` as output/observation, the retained mediator parameter experiment, one compatible Theta and global U, and heat geometry, and forbids boundary exchange and time reversal.

No premise supplies a canonical raw latent realization, a target-erasing comparison category, shared-noise randomization, a noncompact classifier, an uncontrolled null conditional version, an ELBO identity, an autonomous agent, gauge/RG dynamics, or physical ontology.
permitted_theorems: Elementary monoid-congruence and quotient universal-property arguments, with algebraic response-compatible triples, factor-map direction, finite-only cardinality, and quotient-map compatibility proved directly in the package.

Compactness and metrizability of countable products of compact metrizable images; compact-to-Hausdorff continuous bijection; product and quotient-map descent; continuity of finite-coordinate right override with isolated bottom symbols; and compact metrizability of P(T) in the weak topology for compact metrizable T, all with hypotheses mapped directly.

Finite-DAG kernel normalization and polynomial dependence of retained-law coordinates on Euclidean/evaluation-continuous stochastic-kernel coordinates; finite affine convolution; exact rational determinant elimination; total-variation invariance under typed bijections; and the extreme-point theorem for affine simplex bijections.
Finite topological-order Ionescu--Tulcea recursion for declared standard-Borel kernels and continuity of iterated Feller integration on compact Polish spaces.
The circle heat-semigroup law, Fourier diagonalization, and contraction of Markov operators on bounded Fourier modes, each derived or mapped explicitly.

Blackwell comparison as existence of a response-side Markov garbling in the fixed mediator parameter experiment. Exact recomputation may corroborate finite identities but cannot close a mathematical claim.
target.falsification_criterion: A counterexample within a conjunct's frozen hypotheses and ordered-boundary-preserving morphism category to its stated congruence, factorization, finite-only cardinality, quotient topology, normalization, measurability, response continuity, response intertwining, target preservation, contextual rank, or one-way Blackwell conclusion refutes the affirmative conjunction. By contrast, an incomplete derivation, unresolved side condition, missing hypothesis mapping, or missing eligible evidence does not refute the target; it yields INCONCLUSIVE and blocks a complete release. A boundary-reversing presentation is outside the admitted category and neither proves nor refutes the target. Failure of any explicitly excluded raw-realization, target-erasing, correlated, null-version, noncompact, VFE/ELBO, agency, gauge/RG, or ontology extension does not refute this target because those claims are outside closure.
